title: Choose NexaMind's visual world: the familiar end
question: A safer hand: three conventional directions and the category standard. Pick one, or re-roll.

options.label: Swiss Grid
options.lineage: International Typographic Style posters and signage
options.thesis: A strict grid, one confident grotesk and colour used only to say where you are.
options.viewport: Black rail, white work area on a 12-column grid; the page title set large flush-left with the workspace colour as a solid field behind the active nav item.
options.risk: Familiar and clean, but can feel cold if the type scale is timid.

options.label: Paperback Shelf
options.lineage: colour-coded Penguin and Pelican paperback series
options.thesis: Every part of the workspace has its series colour, like a shelf you can read by spine.
options.viewport: Off-white ground, dark rail; each panel carries a thin series band (docs blue, chat cerise, meetings green, tasks ochre) and page headers use the three-band layout.
options.risk: Many colours to keep disciplined; drifts into a rainbow if bands grow beyond thin strips.

options.label: Workshop Pegboard
options.lineage: a maker workshop's tool wall, where every tool has its painted outline
options.thesis: Everything in one place, each with its spot: the workspace as a well-kept tool wall.
options.viewport: A faint pegboard dot grid behind the work area; empty states show the outline of what belongs there; one safety-orange primary action.
options.risk: The least conventional of the three; the dot grid must stay faint or it becomes a costume.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: NexaMind alongside Linear, Notion and Slack, at their level of craft.
canonCard.viewport: Grey sidebar with workspace switcher, white canvas, compact rows and one accent colour.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
